affiliations.date_precision: documented on 1940-12-11; Library of Congress chronology gives circa 1940 and a 1941 wartime transition
affiliations.research_notes: A contemporary December 1940 newspaper identifies Wallace W. Atwood Jr. as Clark University's professor of physiography. The Library of Congress chronology independently places him there circa 1940 and in wartime Army Map Service work from 1941. Clark is therefore the best-supported last civilian employer before wartime service, but it is not labeled the immediate pre-OSS affiliation because the exact Army Map Service and OSS transfer sequence remains unresolved.

affiliations.role_title: assistant in charge of work relating to earth sciences
affiliations.research_notes: The National Park Service's 1940 history names Wallace W. Atwood Jr., describes his earth-sciences responsibility, and dates his successor to March 1932. The Library of Congress finding aid independently summarizes the role as Assistant Chief, 1930-1932. It is earlier documented prewar government work, not the immediate predecessor to OSS.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Major Wallace W. Atwood Jr. is strongly matched to geographer Wallace Walter Atwood Jr., who directed wartime topographic-model work and contributed to the OSS Atcorob.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Named after its inventors, Wallace Atwood, H.L. Cooke, and Arthur Robinson
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Library of Congress supplies his full name and wartime Army topographic-model directorship; CIA identifies Wallace Atwood as an OSS Topographic Model Section inventor.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence: the suffix, W. initial, rare full name, major Army context, geography specialization, wartime topographic-model directorship, and official OSS map-work attribution align across NARA, Library of Congress, and CIA sources.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources establish the wartime identity and map-specialist role. They do not fully resolve whether the Army Map Service label describes an intervening assignment, an overlapping detail, or the same activity as the OSS Topographic Model Section.
claims.match_notes: The full name Wallace Walter Atwood Jr. and 1907-1992 lifespan distinguish the indexed son from Wallace W. Atwood Sr., Clark University's president. Box 25 and Army records remain necessary for direct identifier confirmation.
